facts.statement: The dinosaur Koreaceratops was formally described by Yuong-Nam Lee and colleagues in 2011.
facts.quote: Koreaceratops was described by Yuong-Nam Lee and colleagues in 2011.

facts.statement: The genus name Koreaceratops combines the word 'Korea' with Greek words for 'horn' and 'face'.
facts.quote: The genus name is a combination of "Korea" and the Greek κέρας (keras) meaning 'horn' and ὄψις (opsis) meaning 'face'.

facts.statement: The type specimen consists of an articulated series of 36 tail vertebrae linked to partial hind limbs and ischia.
facts.quote: It is based on KIGAM VP 200801, an articulated series of 36 caudal vertebrae associated with partial hind limbs and ischia.

facts.statement: The fossils were recovered from the Albian-aged Tando beds.
facts.quote: The type specimen came from the Albian-aged Tando beds.

facts.statement: Koreaceratops was a basal ceratopsian dinosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous period in South Korea.
facts.quote: Koreaceratops () is a genus of basal ceratopsian dinosaur discovered in Albian-aged (Early Cretaceous) rocks of South Korea.

facts.statement: The animal lived approximately 103 million years ago during the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 103 millones de años, en el Aptiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: The upper part of the formation containing the fossils is informally dated to 103 ± 0.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: La parte superior de esta formación se fecha de manera informal hace 103 ± 0,5 millones de años.

facts.statement: Koreaceratops is distinguished by the height of the neural spines on its tail vertebrae and the structure of its astragalus bone.
facts.quote: Koreaceratops es notable por la altura de las espinas neurales en las vértebras caudales, y la estructura de su astrágalo.

facts.statement: In some distal tail vertebrae, the neural spines are more than five times the height of the vertebral centra.
facts.quote: En algunas de las vértebras caudales distales, las espinas neurales tienen más de cinco veces la altura de los centros vertebrales a los que se unen.

facts.statement: Researchers have hypothesized that the tall tail spines evolved independently, possibly as an adaptation for swimming.
facts.quote: Lee et al. han postulado que la función se ha desarrollado de forma independiente, tal vez como una adaptación para la natación.

facts.statement: Bone histology analysis suggests the type specimen was about eight years old at death and had not reached physical or sexual maturity.
facts.quote: An examination of the bone histology of Koreaceratops published in 2022 suggests that the type specimen was roughly eight years old when it died and did not reach physical or sexual maturity.

facts.statement: Studies suggest Koreaceratops inhabited a semiarid environment and that microbial erosion caused the poor preservation of its unique features.
facts.quote: The same study suggests that Koreaceratops lived in a semiarid environment, and that microbial erosion is responsible for the poor preservation of its distinguishing features.

facts.statement: Thomas Holtz estimated the length of the type specimen to be 1.3 meters.
facts.quote: Thomas Holtz gave a length estimate of 1.3 m for this specimen.

facts.statement: A phylogenetic analysis by Lee et al. placed Koreaceratops between Archaeoceratops and more derived ceratopsians.
facts.quote: Lee et al. performed a phylogenetic analysis and found Koreaceratops to be positioned between Archaeoceratops and more derived ceratopsians.

facts.statement: A phylogenetic analysis found Koreaceratops to be positioned between Archaeoceratops and more derived ceratopsians.
facts.quote: Lee et al. realizaron un análisis filogenético y encontraron que Koreaceratops puede ser movido entre Archaeoceratops y los ceratopsianos más derivados.

facts.statement: Koreaceratops is classified within the family Archaeoceratopsidae.
The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Koreaceratops as Leptoceratopsidae.
The Paleobi Database classifies Koreaceratops in the family Leptoceratopsidae.
Some researchers exclude Koreaceratops from phylogenetic analyses because the lack of skull material leads to complicated resolution within neoceratopsians.
facts.quote: Some researchers have removed Koreaceratops from phylogenetic analyses due to the lack of skull material from the type specimen which results in a complicated resolution within neoceratopsians.

rejected.statement: A 2022 study suggests Koreaceratops is more closely related to Protoceratops than to earlier animals like Psittacosaurus and Archaeoceratops.
rejected.quote: A 2022 study however, suggests it is closer to Protoceratops than to earlier animals like Psittacosaurus and Archaeoceratops.
